newsitem.title: INDIA: Chidambaram against stronger Indian rupee.
newsitem.headline: Chidambaram against stronger Indian rupee.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Thursday he was against the rupee strengthening further as it would cause problems for exporters.
"I would not like the rupee to strengthen because exporters will then complain," Chidambaram told Reuters in parliament.
The Finance Minister said he was against any action to clip the rupee's strength, and entrusted any necessary intervention to the Reserve Bank of India.
"At the moment I don't think we should try to do anything. We should just leave it to the Reserve Bank, which I think is monitoring the matter carefully."
He said the exchange rate was acceptable "...as long as it is within a band."
Asked whether the exchange rate was within the right band, he replied: "That we leave to the Reserve Bank. Let us see, inflows are very large."
The rupee was quoted at 35.82/83 in late trading against the dollar.
